newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ceramco's Bendon back in profit - Appleby.
newsitem.headline: Ceramco's Bendon back in profit - Appleby.

text.p: Ceramco Corp Ltd's loss-making Bendon-Hickory apparel division returned to profit in the first quarter to June but chairman David Appleby said on Tuesday it would take time to completely turn it around.
Apparel made a NZ$2.61 million loss in the year to March.
Appleby told the annual meeting he expected Bendon's new chief executive, Hugo Venter, to bring Bendon "back to its former glory".
Over the year, the apparel sector in general had been difficult in both Australia and New Zealand, he said.

"Whilst I'm confident that you won't see any brackets alongside the apparel's divisions figures, it would be optimistic of me to say that the division will return to substantial profit quickly," he said.
"We do believe that we have turned the corner and we'll need to monitor that situation."
The division was focusing on customer relationships and would now use its factory shops to clear old stock rather than compete with existing retailers.
Appleby said Ceramco had a struck a new deal with international supermodel, Elle MacPherson, to introduce a line of menswear in November.
The Hickory brand would also be repositioned to have a greater presence in discount department stores.
Ceramco's six month result will report each division on an EBIT basis, in line with analysts' requests.
Ceramco is interviewing candidates to replace Rod Inglis, who resigned a month ago, and is seeking a woman to take a place on the board, Appleby said.
The China Clays business was moving into technical ceramics, which now represent about 10 percent of exports.

The company's "problem child", concrete additive producer Microsilica, remained in loss and helped drag down mining's contribution. It was unlikely Microsilica would become earnings positive in the short term.
Ceramco's menswear company, Clifford John Webster, had been retained after its sale fell through last year and was looking to expand.
Property sales would continue, and Ceramco expects to divest about NZ$3.0 million this year.
In its annual accounts, Ceramco recognised an unusual item in underfunded pensions for former employees.
After tax, the gross cost came to NZ$2.7 million and had been recognised as a long term liability.
Ceramco last traded at NZ$1.75, up two.
